text:
The Penguins are winless in five, outscored 20-9, and the conversation around them has moved to who gets traded. Erik Karlsson and Rickard Rakell lead the rumor mill, with Markerzone relaying Josh Yohe's report that both are about to be moved and Ottawa linked to Rakell. There is talk around Evgeni Malkin's future too, and Sidney Crosby has a contract decision looming. Our playoff odds give Pittsburgh 4.5%.

The frustrating part is that the record is worse than the hockey. Pittsburgh has a -18 goal difference on just -4.5 expected goals (the quality of chances), because its shooters have scored 10.9 fewer goals than their chances usually produce. The goaltending hasn't helped: Arturs Silovs has a .845 save percentage and is 5.9 goals worse than expected over his last five starts, all losses. Bryan Rust and Egor Chinakhov are on injured reserve, and Malkin has moved up beside Crosby and Rakell.

Buffalo just beat the Rangers 5-1, with Rasmus Dahlin scoring 17 seconds in, and The Athletic's Matthew Fairburn asked whether the Sabres might be turning a corner. Tage Thompson has nine points in a five-game streak, Jack Quinn has goals in four straight, and Zach Benson and Jiri Kulich have found a line with Thompson. Alex Lyon starts in goal over Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen, after just four games this season.

Our numbers have Buffalo at 3.53 expected goals and Pittsburgh at 3.15. Our Sleepers come from the Sabres: fourth-liner Jason Zucker at 23% to score, on dangerous chances lately, and Owen Power at 50% for a point. We have Thompson at 44% to score, the highest in this game. At 16 points, Pittsburgh needs a win of any kind; Buffalo, at 26, has a chance to make a good week look like the start of something.
headline: Winless Penguins visit Buffalo amid trade noise
